theme: Incentive travel that earns its ROI before the flight lands

linkedin.text:
Most incentive travel budgets are approved on gut feel. Most post-trip reports measure satisfaction scores.

Neither is wrong — but neither tells you whether the trip moved the needle on the thing that actually mattered: retention, sales performance, cultural alignment.

After 16 years and 1,500+ events, here's what we've seen separate the programs that get renewed from the ones that get cut:

→ The business objective was named before the destination was chosen.
→ The on-ground experience was designed to reinforce that objective — not just fill time between meals.
→ Leadership showed up with a message, not just a presence.

Incentive travel is one of the highest-leverage tools in an HR or sales leader's toolkit. It's also one of the easiest to dilute when planning starts with "where should we go?" instead of "what do we need to achieve?"

If you're scoping a program for your top performers and want a strategic conversation before you go to RFP — my DMs are open.

facebook.text:
The real work of an incentive trip happens long before boarding passes are printed.

When the destination is chosen strategically, the program is built around your team's actual motivators, and every touchpoint reinforces the message you want people to carry home — the ROI shows up in Q4, not just in the group photo.

We've moved 25,000+ participants across 130+ destinations over 16 years. The ones that hit hardest? Always the ones where business intent drove every design decision.

What does ROI look like on your incentive trips? Drop your metric in the comments — curious what other teams are measuring. 👇
